competitorWins: Airplanes.live is pure community ethos: every aircraft every receiver hears is shown, unfiltered and unobfuscated — military jets, Air Force One, special-interest traffic that commercial trackers scrub. Feeders get the unfiltered MLAT results back. For planespotters and researchers who care about seeing the whole sky, including the parts others hide, and for anyone who wants their own receiver to contribute to an open network, it is the free, principled choice.
description: Airplanes.live is a community-run ADS-B/MLAT aggregator fed by enthusiast receivers, showing live traffic exactly as heard — including military and special-interest aircraft that commercial sites block. It is free to use, though its public API is now restricted to feeders. WorldEye is complementary for the casual viewer: free live aircraft on a 3D globe plus ships, cameras, weather, quakes, fires and satellite imagery, with zero community overhead.

tagline: A free, community-run ADS-B and MLAT aggregator that never filters the aircraft other trackers hide.
verdictCompetitor: Choose Airplanes.live if you want a free, community-run, deliberately unfiltered ADS-B map — military traffic included — and are fine with a single-purpose 2D viewer.
verdictWorldEye: Choose WorldEye if you want free live flights on a beautiful globe that also shows ships, cameras, weather and satellite imagery — no signup, no technical setup.
whyWorldEye: Entire globe free with no signup, on a polished 3D map instead of a hobbyist 2D feed.
One view combines flights with ships, ~36,000 cameras, weather, earthquakes, wildfires and satellite imagery.
